audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers say 'trade when Apprehend is down' over and over without ever giving the number, and the one Galio-specific counterplay in the matchup is absent: Justice Punch answers Noxian Guillotine.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 over 535 range — the longest cooldown in the lane by a wide margin, so a missed pull is a 26-second free window, not a vague one. And Noxian Guillotine is a leap: 'Darius leaps to an enemy champion and strikes a lethal blow'. Justice Punch knocks up the first enemy champion it reaches, which is why the punch is worth holding for his commit rather than spending on poke.
audit.corrected: 26s written into the tldr, winCon, stage lines, cooldown block, do's and all-in windows; the Guillotine denial written into the don'ts, the level-6 stage and the key-interactions slot.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why calls Stormsurge/Riftmaker your spike on a stage the chart gives Darius, phases[4].why ends with the boilerplate 'Reassess his ultimate too', and phases[6].why is the same 'best teamfight button in the game' filler used on every other matchup.
audit.why: His spikes are Apprehend at 3, five Hemorrhage stacks into Noxian Might, and his first dive item. Decimate is 9s at rank 1 and Crippling Strike a flat 5s — those are the rotation timers a Galio can count.
audit.corrected: Stage lines rebuilt on those numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[2] reads 'His early — survive to your spikes' but the chart gives Darius the two item stages as well, i.e. the end of the game.
audit.why: The recorded stages are Skill at 1, Darius at 2 and 3, Skill at 4-5 and 6, Darius at both item rows. Calling it 'his early' misreads the shape of the lane the page itself draws.
audit.corrected: Chart summary rewritten to state the actual split; the stages themselves left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization says 'Oblivion Orb early — his healing fights your trade math' without naming the heal, and offers boots as a coin flip.
audit.why: The heal is Decimate: 'Darius heals based on enemy champions and large monsters hit by the blade' — the outer edge, on a 9s rank-1 cooldown. His damage is physical apart from the true-damage ultimate, so Plated Steelcaps is the boot and raw resistances are the wrong answer to Noxian Guillotine.
audit.corrected: Heal source named, boots resolved, and the true-damage caveat added to the 2+ items stage and the mistakes list.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing gives the tell for his burst opener.
audit.why: Crippling Strike is an auto-attack reset on a flat 5s cooldown — the wind-up on his basic attack is the cue to disengage, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: Written into the Levels 4-5 stage line.

edits.before: Do not brawl Darius levels 1-3 — you start with a single ability and no real engage, and his Apprehend (E) pull into stacked Hemorrhage bleed plus a sweet-spot Decimate wins every melee exchange in this window, especially once five stacks trigger Noxian Might. Last-hit with the windblast tips of Winds of War from outside his E range and accept the lane is his. The one thing he must respect: if he steps up to Apprehend, pre-charge Shield of Durand so the taunt fires the instant he pulls, then Justice Punch out — that breaks the all-in instead of feeding his bleed.

The blade edge of Decimate also heals him, so poke does not stick without Oblivion Orb. Last-hit with the windblast tips of Winds of War from outside Apprehend's 535 range and accept the lane is his. The one thing he must respect: if he steps up to pull, pre-charge Shield of Durand so the taunt fires the instant he lands it, then Justice Punch out.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are where you stabilize, but never on his terms. Your Shield of Durand taunt into a Justice Punch knockup can punish a whiffed Apprehend, but if his Hemorrhage is stacked into Noxian Might he still out-damages your return, so only commit when his E is on cooldown and you have Winds of War poke layered first. The real swing is Level 6: Hero's Entrance is a global, so the correct play in a losing lane is to flag into mid or bot and land your taunt-knockup on a fight while Darius is stuck shoving a wave alone — your value is the map, not the duel.

Your Shield of Durand taunt into a Justice Punch knockup can punish a whiffed Apprehend — 26s at rank 1, so a miss is a real window — but if Hemorrhage is stacked into Noxian Might he still out-damages your return. From 6, save the punch for his Noxian Guillotine: it is a leap, and a knockup is what stops it. The real swing is Hero's Entrance, a global, so in a losing lane you flag into mid or bot and land your taunt-knockup while Darius shoves a wave alone.

edits.before: This is the only window that tilts your way. By 2+ items your tank-AP build, Shield of Durand's heavy damage reduction, and raw HP let you sponge his full all-in — your effective health pool pushes the Noxian Guillotine execute threshold out of reach — while Darius's solo-kill pressure plateaus. You will never out-duel him cleanly, but you don't have to: you out-team-fight him with Shield of Durand peel and Hero's Entrance picks. Group up, and never get caught split-pushing alone into him where his Apprehend-to-Guillotine can isolate you.
